prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1272; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim purposes. Can you confirm you're okay to proceed?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Great. Can you walk me through what happened on the day of the collision?

A: I was driving on a two-lane road in Houston, heading toward the highway. It was a fairly quiet stretch. Traffic was light, and I was going maybe twenty-five miles an hour.

Q: Where were you when you first noticed the other vehicle?

A: The other car was coming toward me in my lane. It had drifted over the center line. I tapped the brakes and turned to the right, but it still hit my front end. It wasn't a hard impact, more like a bump and a jolt.

Q: Did either airbag deploy?

A: No, they didn't. My seatbelt was on, and I didn't hit my head.

Q: Can you describe your injuries?

A: My left wrist hurt right away. I put my hand out on the steering wheel and it took most of the force. I went to the emergency room later that day and they said it was fractured. I've got a cast and I'm seeing a specialist next week.

Q: Are you still receiving treatment?

A: Yes, I'm doing physical therapy twice a week for now. I haven't been able to drive much since, and I've had to rely on rides from family.

Q: Did you have any prior injuries to that wrist?

A: No, nothing I can remember.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add about the accident?

A: Just that the other driver apologized at the scene and said they had looked down at their phone. I wanted that on record.

Q: Thank you. We'll follow up with you in writing about the next steps.

A: Okay, thank you.
